issues.title: Validator Rules (batch one0
issues.body:
The first batch - 8pm here, more tomorrow.

FIrst, great set of rules - there are a lot of duplicates in there which I'm sure you've spotted, but it's a very useful list.

I've now gone through both the list, and the impementation report from `validator_web.py`, so here a mixed bag of issues which may be in the list and/or in the implementation

***Rules 25, 29, 30, 31, 32***. Any requirements around NonFullScreenPageMode are silly as, by the definition of ISO32000, they are required to be ignored. See https://github.com/pdf-association/report-an-issue/issues/14, and definition in ISO32000-2:2020 Table 147 on page 438. We are currently not enforcing this for this reason, but it will be zero cost for us to add the rule to our generator so we'll do that - the path of least resistance, etc.

***Rule 38***. This is manifesting as "Leaf DPart Start/End do not resolve to pages" in the validator - but while "Start" is required and must be a page, "End" is not required if the part is only one page long (ie. it defaults to the same value as "Start". See the definition in ISO32000-2:2020 Table 490 on page 837

***Rule 96***: checking that the root element of the StructTreeRoot - the "K" - is a Document, needs to take into account that it may be another element that is _role-mapped_ to Document. RoleMapping for PDF 1.7 is pretty simple, if the tag name isn't one you expect then look it up in the /RoleMap key on the StructTreeRoot. RoleMapping for PDF 2.0 is more complex, you need to look in the "NS" object for the element, then the "RoleMapNS" key, then look up the value in there.

***Rule 142***: you're confirming there's a namespace declaration for `xmlns:pdfmail="http://www.pdfa.org/eapdf/"` but this isn't in the spec, just `pdfmailid` and `pdfmailmeta`

***Rule 145, 146***: dc:creator is definitely the document author (see https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/elements11/creator/) and xmp:CreateDate is definitely "The date and time the resource was created. For a digital file, this need not match a file-system creation time. For a freshly created resource, it should be close to that time, modulo the time taken to write the file. Later file transfer, copying, and so on, can make the file-system time arbitrarily different." (from ISO16684, the XMP spec). The meaning of these fields is also defined in PDF/A-3, in terms of mapping them to their equivalent valid in the Info dictionary. ***EDIT*** this is actually ***Rule 150, 152***

issues.title: thinkbox.pdf
issues.body:
We're off!

I'm working through your list but step one is I've had a look at the `compare/thinkbox.pdf` and there are some issues in there, so I'll list those out here. 

### Document Parts
The main issue we have with is the Document Parts structure. These are the objects in your file that are part of the DPart tree, which has a root object of "5 0 obj"

```
 5 0 obj << /DPartRootNode 14 0 R >>
12 0 obj << /Type /Page ... /DPart 26 0 obj >>
14 0 obj << /DParts 27 0 R >>
27 0 obj << /DPM 36 0 R /DParts 26 0 R >>
26 0 obj << /DPM 35 0 R /Start 12 0 R /End 12 0 R >>
35 0 obj << /Mail_ContentSetType (BodyRendering) /Mail_Subtype (text/html) /Mail_Desc (Message body) >>
36 0 obj << /Mail_GUID (...) /Mail_MessageID (...) >>
```

There are two main problems here:
1. `/DParts` must be an array of arrays (weird, yes)
2. Every intermediate node must have a pointer to its parent

It should look like this:

```
 5 0 obj << /DPartRootNode 14 0 R >>
12 0 obj << /Type /Page ... /DPart 26 0 obj >>
14 0 obj << /Parent 5 0 R /DParts [ [ 27 0 R ] ] >>
27 0 obj << /Parent 14 0 R /DPM 36 0 R /DParts [ [ 26 0 R ] ] >>
26 0 obj << /Paernt 27 0 R /DPM 35 0 R /Start 12 0 R /End 12 0 R >>
35 0 obj << /Mail_ContentSetType (BodyRendering) /Mail_Subtype (text/html) /Mail_Desc (Message body) >>
36 0 obj << /Mail_GUID (...) /Mail_MessageID (...) >>
```

### CIDSet
 in PDF/A-4, the `CIDSet` key is not allowed on fonts (it's required in earlier versions of PDF/A, but is now banned).

### Checksum
It's a warning not an error, but the checksum on the EmbeddedFile is defined as MD5, so it has to be 16 chars long :smile:

### Tags
The tags in the PDF StructureTree aren't actually tagging any content on the page! You'd need to wrap some content on the page with Marked Content sequences eg `/Span <</MCID 0>>`, then refer to that MCID from the `K` array in the tree. There's more to it of course, but that's the broad outline. Tags are optional, you could do worse than... not tagging your PDF.

Those are the "red flags" - and don't worry, your validator has found a few in our file too...

2.body:
A few more:

***Rule 47***: it looks like `validate_eapdf.py` is looking for attachments under the `BodyRendering` DPart; they should be under the `AttachmentList` DPart

And to expand on the "Rule 96" issue above, I can see in your `thinkbox.pdf` you're using PDF 1.x style rolemapping, which is probably what your validator is looking for. Rolemapping in PDF 2.x is different - the `RoleMap` key is ignored. I know what we're doing is correct because we talked it over at length with Matthew Hardy back in the early days of PDF/UA-2 (and what we're doing is validated by other tools like veraPDF). I suspect this is the reason behind a few of the issues your validator has with our sample file attached below.

But that's all - I've now finished going through the issue list, and nothing else contentious jumps out.

---

I think the most interesting one is the definition of `xmp:CreateDate` - is the "date and time the resource was created" referring to the PDF or the Email? I could be swayed either way, but I think on balance I agree with you - it's the time the PDF was created.

This is certainly something that should be clarified for version 1.1 of the spec, and in particular I'm not convinced the claim that the field SHALL be the PDF creation date is present in the spec - meaning I don't think you could enforce this as a validation rule.

As a result of all this we've now applied some fixes to our code:
* we're enforcing ISO32005 compliance on our PDF/A-4 tagged documents and adding the declaration that we do so, although I'm not convinced it's a good idea (https://github.com/pdf-association/report-an-issue/issues/21)
* we've changed the revision date from 2025 to 2024
* we're setting the Mail_GUID attribute on the root element in the tagged PDF, although your validator doesn't seem to be finding it (see note on Rule 96 above)
* we're setting the `NonFullScreenPageMode`, under protest :smile:
* we're now setting xmp:CreateDate to the PDF-creation time, not the email-sent time
* we've corrected the nesting of the tags - Mail_Message is now the outer tag, not Mail_ContentGroup
 
I'm attaching an updated sample. [sample.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26435040/out.pdf) - your validator still has some issues with this, but I think these are all validator bugs mentioned previously.
